summary: Most nationalities need a visa for Guinea-Bissau before they travel, issued by its embassies (for example in Paris and Lisbon). An eVisa and a visa on arrival at Bissau airport have been offered, but no official source currently confirms them. ECOWAS citizens enter freely under the bloc's free-movement protocol.

fee.notes: 90-day visa. A 45-day visa is EUR 70 and a 180-day visa EUR 200, applied for in person at a mission such as the embassies in Paris or Lisbon. These are the fees Ireland's foreign ministry quotes for Irish citizens; other nationalities may pay differently.

travelInsurance.text: No official source states a travel-insurance requirement for entry to Guinea-Bissau. Ireland's foreign ministry calls comprehensive travel insurance essential, and Canada advises cover that includes medical evacuation.

currencyLimits.text: You may bring in any amount of foreign currency provided you declare it on arrival; you can take out no more than you declared. Importing or exporting the local currency is prohibited, according to the Government of Canada.

source.name: Government of Canada — Guinea-Bissau travel advice and advisories

payments.text: Guinea-Bissau is a cash economy. Cards are accepted at only one or two Bissau hotels and reliable ATMs are scarce. Bring euros in cash to exchange; the CFA franc is pegged to the euro.

safety.text: Guinea-Bissau suffers from political instability. Avoid demonstrations, large gatherings and sensitive areas such as military installations and government buildings. Pickpocketing and bag and phone snatching are relatively common in Bissau, and landmines remain a risk outside the capital, so stay on paved roads there.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Guinea-Bissau travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to April is the dry season — the best window for Bissau and boat trips to the Bijagós archipelago; heavy rains from June to October cut off much of the country.

tips.text: No official source currently confirms the eVisa or the airport visa on arrival, and neither would help at a land border. If you are entering by land from Senegal or Guinea, get a visa from a Guinea-Bissau embassy (for example in Dakar or Conakry) before you travel.
The Bijagós islands — the country's main draw — are reached by boat from Bissau; services are informal and weather-dependent, so build slack into your itinerary.
Bring all the money you need as cash, ideally euros. The CFA franc is pegged to the euro and exchange in Bissau is straightforward, while ATMs and card payments cannot be relied on.
Guinea-Bissau has a long history of coups and political crises. Avoid protests, checkpoints arguments and the areas around government and military buildings, and monitor the news during your stay.

The site that operates Guinea-Bissau's electronic visa application, rgb-visa.com, is currently serving injected advertising links for gambling sites alongside its own content, which is the signature of a compromised web server. We have removed our link to it. Until it is cleaned up, arrange the visa through a Guinea-Bissau embassy or the letter-of-authorisation route for arrival at Bissau airport, and do not enter passport or card details on that site.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Guinea-Bissau?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do, and it should be arranged before you fly: Guinea-Bissau's embassies (for example in Paris and Lisbon) issue visas in person; Ireland's foreign ministry quotes Irish citizens EUR 70 for 45 days, EUR 110 for 90 days or EUR 200 for 180 days. An eVisa and an airport visa on arrival have been offered, but no official source currently confirms them. Citizens of the 15 ECOWAS countries are exempt and enter freely under the bloc's free-movement protocol.

faq.question: How does the visa on arrival in Guinea-Bissau work?
faq.answer: No official source we can check confirms a visa on arrival for Guinea-Bissau. The UK government says visitors must have a visa and should apply through the Guinea-Bissau Embassy in Paris, or an embassy in a neighbouring country such as Senegal. Get the visa before you travel, especially if you are arriving overland.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Guinea-Bissau?
faq.answer: Yes. You must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Guinea-Bissau.

faq.question: Is Guinea-Bissau safe to visit?
faq.answer: Day-to-day crime against visitors is low, but the country is politically fragile with a history of coup attempts. Most trips — especially to the Bijagós islands — are trouble-free; avoid demonstrations and check your government's travel advice before booking.

faq.question: Can I pay by card in Guinea-Bissau?
faq.answer: Effectively no. Bring cash — ideally euros, which exchange easily into the euro-pegged CFA franc. Cards work at only a couple of hotels in Bissau and ATMs are few and unreliable.
